changes.description: Added new code for clauses establishing professional/design liability insurance requirements and a design-services-specific liability cap, distinct from the general liability cap and general insurance regime.
changes.justification: CCDC 14 GC 11.1.1.9 mandates dedicated professional liability insurance for the Design-Builder (a requirement absent from CCDC 2/3/5A/5B, which allocate design responsibility to a separately-retained Consultant outside the construction contract), and GC 12.3 establishes a distinct liability cap specifically for claims arising from the Design Services (tied to that insurance and limited to errors/omissions of the Consultant/Other Consultants). This dual mechanism is a direct product of the design-build delivery model's integration of design and construction risk within a single contracting party, and is clause-level identifiable and comparatively useful (Rule 1-3): it lets researchers compare how different CCDC forms allocate and insure design risk for MMC/prefab projects where design and fabrication are closely coupled.

changes.description: Added CCDC 14 as a design-build (single point of responsibility) delivery structure comparator.
changes.justification: CCDC 14 vests the Design-Builder with 'total control of the Design Services and of the Work' (GC 3.1.1) and requires the Design-Builder to contract with the Consultant (not the Owner) under a CCDC 15-based agreement (GC 3.1.3-3.1.4), making the Design-Builder fully responsible to the Owner for the Consultant's acts (GC 3.1.6). This is the paradigmatic single-point design-build structure referenced in the literature's DB-as-integrator category, contrasting with CCDC 2's DBB split and CCDC 3/5A/5B's CM structures.

changes.description: Clarified that CCDC 14 contains no explicit ECI/two-stage/PCSA mechanism distinct from its underlying design-build structure.
changes.justification: CCDC 14's integration of design and construction responsibility in a single Design-Builder (see C1) inherently enables earlier design-fabrication coordination than DBB, but the form contains no discrete two-stage tendering, PCSA, or nominated-supplier clause of the kind this code targets; absence is a valid comparative result distinguishing structural integration (C1) from an explicit contractual ECI mechanism (C2).

changes.description: Added CCDC 14's staged design-review/acceptance mechanism and allowance provisions as design-finalization-adjacent clauses.
changes.justification: GC 2.5.1-2.5.4 requires the Owner to review design development documents and proposed Construction Documents against a jointly agreed schedule and to advise acceptance or rejection within 10 days, functioning as a staged design-finalization gate distinct from the traditional single design-freeze point in DBB forms; GC 4.1 (Cash Allowances) and GC 4.2 (Contingency Allowance) mirror CCDC 2/3/5B's deferral mechanism permitting scope to remain undefined at signing.

changes.description: Confirmed CCDC 14's Work/Products scope definition additionally encompasses 'design' as an integrated deliverable.
changes.justification: GC 1.1.1 defines Contract Documents' intent to include 'the design, the labour, the Products and other services necessary for the design and performance of the Work,' extending CCDC 2/3/5B's Work/Products definitional anchor to expressly incorporate design as a bundled deliverable, consistent with the design-build delivery model.

changes.description: Added CCDC 14 progress/final payment anchors including payment for the Design Services component.
changes.justification: GC 5.2.3 and GC 5.2.8 parallel CCDC 2/3/5B's Products-delivered-but-not-incorporated payment mechanics, but explicitly extend the payment basis to include 'the value...of the Design Services and of the Work performed,' reflecting the bundled design-construction payment stream unique to design-build forms.

changes.description: Confirmed CCDC 14's holdback mechanics parallel other CCDC forms; no liquidated damages clause present.
changes.justification: GC 5.5 (Payment of Holdback Upon Substantial Performance) and GC 5.6 (Progressive Release of Holdback) are materially parallel to CCDC 2/3/5B's holdback regimes, including the common-law/Quebec bifurcation (GC 5.5.4-5.5.5); no stipulated liquidated damages clause is present, consistent with other CCDC forms reviewed.

changes.description: Confirmed CCDC 14's Change Directive valuation mechanism includes shop/expediting labour cost recovery within the change-valuation clause itself (not a separate Cost-of-the-Work definition).
changes.justification: GC 6.3.7 (referenced cost categories for Change Directive valuation) parallels CCDC 2's GC 6.3.7 structure, situating shop/factory labour and expediting cost recovery directly within the change-valuation mechanism rather than within a baseline reimbursable-cost definition as in CCDC 3/5B (C37), confirming CCDC 14 patterns with the stipulated-price forms on this boundary.

changes.description: Confirmed materially identical Concealed/Unknown Conditions and force-majeure-type delay anchors in CCDC 14.
changes.justification: GC 6.4 (Concealed or Unknown Conditions) and GC 6.5.3 (labour disputes, fire, weather, causes beyond Design-Builder's control) are materially identical in structure to CCDC 2/3/5B's equivalent clauses, confirming recurrence of this clause type in the design-build form.

changes.description: Confirmed identical changes-in-law claims mechanism.
changes.justification: GC 10.2.7 (claims for changes to laws/codes after proposal/bid closing, routed through GC 6.6 claims mechanism) parallels CCDC 2/3/5B's equivalent provision.

changes.description: Added CCDC 14's balancing/disclaimer clauses, including its distinctive dual liability-cap structure (general liability cap plus a separate, narrower design-services liability cap).
changes.justification: GC 3.1.2 (Design-Builder solely responsible for means/methods) and GC 2.1.2-2.1.3 (Design-Builder entitled to rely on Owner-supplied information; not responsible for design errors in Owner-supplied designs absent acceptance) are relevant balancing clauses. Distinctively, GC 12.2.2 sets a general liability cap (insurance limit, or greater of Contract Price/$2,000,000 up to $20,000,000) while GC 12.3.1 sets a separate, narrower cap specifically for claims arising from the Design Services, limited to insurance coverage and to errors of the Consultant/Other Consultants -- a two-tier risk-allocation structure unique to this design-build form and cross-referenced to new code C39.

changes.description: Confirmed CCDC 14's document-priority/amendment-practice anchor is materially identical to other CCDC forms.
changes.justification: GC 1.1.6 sets an order of priority (Agreement, Definitions, Supplementary Conditions, General Conditions, Owner's Statement of Requirements, Construction Documents) materially consistent with the amendment-practice mechanism identified across the CCDC suite.

changes.description: Confirmed absence of a dedicated transit/logistics/insurance clause in CCDC 14.
changes.justification: CCDC 14 contains no dedicated transit/logistics clause beyond the generic reference to 'transportation' as a Design-Builder-provided facility (GC 3.8.1); absence of a dedicated logistics clause is a valid comparative result consistent with CCDC 2/3/5A/5B.

changes.description: Confirmed CCDC 14's explicit factory-access/off-site inspection provision.
changes.justification: GC 3.1.10 explicitly requires the Design-Builder to provide access to 'the Work, including parts being performed at locations other than the Place of the Work,' directly paralleling CCDC 2/3/5B's GC 2.3.1/2.4.1 factory-access QA provisions and confirming this MMC-relevant clause type recurs in the design-build form.

changes.description: Confirmed absence of a chain-of-custody/traceability mechanism in CCDC 14.
changes.justification: CCDC 14 contains no explicit component-traceability or chain-of-custody mechanism; absence is a valid comparative result consistent with all other CCDC forms reviewed.

changes.description: Confirmed CCDC 14's document-ownership clauses do not address BIM/digital model authorship specifically.
changes.justification: GC 1.1.7-1.1.10 address ownership/copyright of the Consultant's or Other Consultant's plans, Drawings, electronic media and models (vesting copyright in the Consultant/Other Consultants rather than the Design-Builder or Owner), a materially more elaborated ownership regime than CCDC 2/3/5B given the design-build model's reliance on a Design-Builder-retained Consultant, but still without addressing BIM/digital model authorship, licensing, or 2D-vs-3D bindingness specifically.

changes.description: Confirmed CCDC 14's analogous liability mechanism for design/fabrication documentation remains its Shop Drawing regime and the newly identified design-services liability cap (C39), rather than a digital-model-specific clause.
changes.justification: CCDC 14 contains no BIM/digital-model-specific liability clause; its Shop Drawing regime (GC 3.10, see C36) and its distinct design-services liability cap (GC 12.3.1, see C11/C39) are the relevant analogues, confirming the same absence-of-digital-model-liability-clause finding as other CCDC forms while highlighting the design-build form's additional design-liability layer.

changes.description: Confirmed CCDC 14 is a bilateral, non-IPD instrument.
changes.justification: CCDC 14 is a bilateral Owner-Design-Builder agreement (Article A-1) with no multiparty signature, shared risk-reward pool, or joint-governance mechanism; absence of IPD/alliance features is a valid comparative result consistent with CCDC 2/3/5A/5B.

changes.description: Added CCDC 14's phase-differentiated suspension/termination structure distinguishing a pre-construction (design-only) suspension mechanism from construction-phase termination.
changes.justification: GC 7.1 creates a distinctive pre-Work-commencement suspension/termination mechanism applicable specifically 'before the Work commences at the Place of the Work' (GC 7.1.1-7.1.4), entitling the Design-Builder to payment for Design Services performed plus damages including reasonable profit if deemed terminated after a 20-Working-Day suspension -- a design-phase-specific termination compensation mechanism distinct from, though structurally related to, CCDC 5B's phase-differentiated compensation split (see C19 CCDC 5B memo). GC 7.2 (Owner's termination for default) and GC 7.3 (Design-Builder's termination rights) parallel CCDC 2/3/5B's symmetric structures.

changes.description: Confirmed CCDC 14's foundational privity clause.
changes.justification: GC 1.1.2 (no contractual relationship between Owner and Consultant, Other Consultant, Subcontractor, Supplier or their agents/employees) is the parallel foundational privity clause to CCDC 2/3/5B's equivalent provisions, notably extended here to expressly include the Consultant given the design-build structure.

changes.description: Confirmed CCDC 14's tiered dispute resolution mechanism is materially identical to other current-generation CCDC forms.
changes.justification: Part 8 (Negotiation, Mediation and Arbitration) requires appointment of a Project Mediator under CCDC 40 within 20 Working Days (GC 8.1.5), followed by mediation and arbitration (GC 8.1.6-8.1.9), with statutory lien rights preserved without waiver of arbitration rights (GC 8.2.2) -- materially identical to CCDC 3/5A/5B's tiered structure.

changes.description: No material drafting-quality anomaly identified in CCDC 14 beyond noting general applicability of the code.
changes.justification: CCDC 14's Part 12 (Indemnification, Limitation of Liability, Waiver of Claims and Warranty) is a lengthy, cross-referential drafting structure (GC 12.1-12.5) illustrating the kind of complex, cross-referencing drafting this code is designed to capture when assessing interpretability across CCDC forms.

changes.description: Confirmed CCDC 14's general communication-formality clause and centralized-communication requirement.
changes.justification: Article A-6 (Notices in Writing) sets general communication formalities paralleling CCDC 2/3/5A/5B; GC 2.2.2 and GC 2.4.6 additionally require that all communications between the Owner/Payment Certifier and the Consultant, Other Consultant, Subcontractor or Supplier be forwarded through the Design-Builder, establishing a centralized-communication-channel requirement analogous to CCDC 5A's GC 3.1.1.8.

changes.description: Added CCDC 14's flow-down and coordination provisions, including its Design-Builder responsibility for Other Consultants alongside Subcontractors/Suppliers.
changes.justification: GC 1.1.2 (no privity) and GC 2.6 (Work by Owner or Other Contractors, including coordination duties and change-order consequences) parallel CCDC 2/3/5B's equivalent provisions. GC 3.4.1 additionally requires the Design-Builder to flow down contract terms not only to Subcontractors/Suppliers but also to Other Consultants, and to be fully responsible for their acts -- an expanded flow-down scope reflecting the design-build model's incorporation of design-services subcontracting.

changes.description: Confirmed CCDC 14 defers bonding/security to separately referenced contract security documents.
changes.justification: GC 11.2.1-11.2.2 address Contract security only where 'specified in the Contract Documents,' referencing CCDC-approved bond forms rather than mandating bonding directly in the General Conditions, consistent with CCDC 2/3/5B's approach. GC 5.1 (Financing Information Required of the Owner) parallels CCDC 3's/5A's financing-assurance provisions running from Owner to Design-Builder.

changes.description: Confirmed absence of smart-contract/automated payment provisions.
changes.justification: CCDC 14 contains no automated/blockchain-based payment or penalty enforcement provisions; absence is a valid comparative result consistent with other CCDC forms reviewed.

changes.description: Confirmed CCDC 14's fixed Contract Price with tax/duty-only adjustment mechanism.
changes.justification: GC 10.1.1-10.1.2 fix the Contract Price inclusive of taxes/duties in effect at proposal/bid closing, with adjustment only for changes in included taxes/duties (via the GC 6.6 claims mechanism), not general material/labour inflation -- confirming the same gap identified in CCDC 2.

changes.description: Confirmed CCDC 14's generic regulatory-compliance clause without modular-specific standards reference.
changes.justification: GC 10.2.1-10.2.7 (Laws, Notices, Permits and Fees) is materially identical in structure to CCDC 2/3/5B's GC 10.2, drafted generically without reference to modular-specific standards, and notably allocates responsibility for verifying the Owner's Statement of Requirements' code-compliance away from the Design-Builder (GC 10.2.5) while requiring the Design-Builder to comply with codes affecting the Design Services/Work.

changes.description: Confirmed CCDC 14's labour-dispute reference functions only as a delay-excusing event.
changes.justification: GC 6.5.3.1 references labour disputes, strikes and lock-outs only as a delay-excusing event, not as a work-allocation mechanism, materially identical to CCDC 2/3/5B's equivalent provision.

changes.description: Confirmed absence of a component-delivery-specific incentive/penalty mechanism.
changes.justification: GC 3.6.1 (Design Services and Work Schedule) requires a schedule and monthly monitoring but contains no component-delivery-specific incentive/penalty mechanism, consistent with CCDC 2/3/5A/5B.

changes.description: Confirmed CCDC 14 is a single-project agreement.
changes.justification: CCDC 14 is drafted as a single-project design-build agreement (Article A-1); absence of framework/serial contracting structures is a valid comparative result consistent with other CCDC forms reviewed.

changes.description: Added CCDC 14's elaborated multi-tier insurance regime and warranty clause, framed around the Place of the Work.
changes.justification: GC 9.1.1 (Protection of Work and Property) and GC 11.1.1 (general liability, automobile, aircraft/watercraft, 'all risks' property, boiler/machinery, equipment, and professional liability insurance, jointly naming Owner, Consultant, Other Consultants, Owner's Advisor and Payment Certifier as insureds) establish a more elaborated regime than CCDC 2/3, closer to CCDC 5A/5B's multi-party structure, but still framed around the Place of the Work and 'the Work,' leaving the same off-site fabrication-facility/in-transit coverage ambiguity identified across the CCDC suite. GC 12.5 (Warranty) parallels CCDC 2/3/5B's one-year warranty anchor. The dedicated professional liability insurance requirement (GC 11.1.1.9) is a design-build-specific addition now cross-referenced to new code C39.

changes.description: Confirmed CCDC 14's nomination/objection/substitution mechanism, extended to Other Consultants.
changes.justification: GC 3.4.2-3.4.5 establish a mechanism closely paralleling CCDC 2/3/5B's Subcontractor/Supplier nomination-objection-substitution provisions, but distinctively extend it to 'Other Consultants' as well, with price/time adjustment consequences for Owner-required changes -- reflecting the design-build model's incorporation of design-services subcontracting into the same qualification/selection framework as construction subcontracting.

changes.description: Clarified that CCDC 14, while a single-point design-build responsibility structure, does not itself constitute a vertically integrated single-entity model since the Consultant remains a separate contracting party retained by the Design-Builder.
changes.justification: CCDC 14 assumes distinct Owner, Consultant, Other Consultant and Design-Builder roles (Article A-1.2, GC 3.1.3-3.1.4), with the Consultant contracted separately under a CCDC 15-based agreement rather than being an in-house function of a single vertically integrated firm; this is a materially different point on the integration spectrum from true single-firm vertical integration, though closer to it than CCDC 2/3/5A/5B's fully separated Owner/Consultant/Contractor structures -- a useful intermediate comparator.

changes.description: Confirmed CCDC 14's scope/roles clauses, drafted without reference to multiple manufacturers/suppliers.
changes.justification: GC 1.1.1-1.1.3 (intent of Contract Documents, complementary documents) are the general anchor clauses, extended to include 'design' given the design-build structure, but drafted without specific reference to multiple manufacturers/suppliers or prefabrication-context role allocation, consistent with other CCDC forms reviewed.

changes.description: Confirmed CCDC 14's Shop Drawing regime is materially identical to other CCDC forms, with review standard framed as conformity to 'the intent of the Contract Documents' rather than 'the design concept.'
changes.justification: GC 3.10.1-3.10.5 establish a fully elaborated Shop Drawing regime paralleling CCDC 2/3/5B's equivalent provisions, confirming the Owner's review is 'for conformity to the intent of the Contract Documents and for general arrangement only' and does not relieve the Design-Builder of responsibility for errors or omissions (GC 3.10.5) -- a design-build-specific rewording ('intent of the Contract Documents' rather than 'design concept') reflecting that the Design-Builder itself, rather than a separately-retained Owner's Consultant, holds primary design responsibility.

codebook.label: Delivery Method/Project Structure Clause
codebook.definition: The contractual framework establishing the overall project delivery structure (design-bid-build, design-build, CM, IPD multiparty, EPC/turnkey) and the resulting allocation of design, procurement and construction responsibility.
codebook.memo: Combines T1's comparative delivery-method codes (DBB unsuitability, DB as integrator, IPD as optimal, EPC/turnkey single-point responsibility, CM-GC options), T5's 'Project Delivery Method Choice' category, T7's procurement/delivery selection category, T9's 'collaborative delivery methods as relational mechanisms', and T12's 'Delivery System Influence' code. CCDC 2 is a paradigmatic single-prime, design-bid-build stipulated-price form. CCDC 2 CcQ retains this same structure for Quebec civil law. CCDC 3 is a CM-for-fee (at-risk) structure with an optional execution plan and GMP/Target Contract Price mechanisms. CCDC 5A is an agency-style CM model with no privity with Trade Contractors. CCDC 5B is an at-risk CM structure with a distinct Pre-construction Services phase and subsequent at-risk Construction Services phase. CCDC 14 is the paradigmatic single-point design-build structure: the Design-Builder holds 'total control of the Design Services and of the Work' (GC 3.1.1) and contracts directly with the Consultant under a CCDC 15-based agreement (GC 3.1.3-3.1.4), bearing full responsibility to the Owner for the Consultant's acts (GC 3.1.6) -- confirming the DB-as-integrator delivery point referenced in the literature and providing the key comparator to CCDC 2's DBB baseline for how design and construction responsibility are unified under one contracting party.

codebook.label: Early Contractor/Manufacturer Involvement Provisions
codebook.definition: Clauses establishing mechanisms (ECI, two-stage tendering, preconstruction services agreements, nominated supplier/strategic partnering terms) that bring contractors, fabricators or manufacturers into the design process before final pricing.
codebook.memo: Merges T1's two-stage/ECI category, T7's 'Contractual Mechanisms for Early Involvement' category, T9's 'Early Involvement and Design-Phase Collaboration', and related codes from T5 and T12 on PCSAs and early engagement. CCDC 2/CcQ and CCDC 3 contain no ECI/two-stage mechanism. CCDC 5A's Pre-Construction Phase fee implies early CM involvement without an explicit mechanism. CCDC 5B provides the clearest explicit ECI-style mechanism via its Pre-construction Services phase. CCDC 14 likewise contains no discrete two-stage tendering, PCSA, or nominated-supplier clause; its structural integration of design and construction responsibility in a single Design-Builder (see C1) inherently enables earlier design-fabrication coordination than DBB, but this is a delivery-structure feature captured under C1 rather than an explicit contractual ECI mechanism -- absence of a dedicated C2-type clause is a valid comparative result.

codebook.label: Design Freeze and Late-Change Consequence Clause
codebook.definition: Provisions setting deadlines for design finalization prior to fabrication and specifying the cost/schedule consequences and approval processes for changes made after that point, including allowance-based mechanisms that permit deferral of design decisions.
codebook.include_when: Apply when a clause establishes (or by mechanism implies) a point at which design/scope must be fixed, or when a clause (e.g., cash/contingency allowances) formally permits deferring finalization of scope/design to a later date with defined cost-adjustment consequences.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to ordinary variation valuation mechanics that do not concern timing of design finalization (see C7), nor to general change-order procedure absent a timing/finalization dimension.
codebook.memo: Combines T2, T7, T8, T9, T12 and T13 design-freeze/late-change codes. CCDC 2/CcQ's and CCDC 3's Cash/Contingency Allowances (GC 4.1/4.2) permit scope to remain undefined at signing. CCDC 5A's termination-compensation formula ties damages to estimating-stage maturity. CCDC 5B's Cash Allowances mirror CCDC 2/3, with a hybrid design-maturity/loss-of-profit termination formula. CCDC 14 contains a staged design-review/acceptance mechanism functioning as a design-finalization gate: GC 2.5.1-2.5.4 requires the Owner to review design development documents and proposed Construction Documents against an agreed schedule and to advise acceptance or rejection within 10 days, with rejected documents requiring Design-Builder revision -- a repeated-gate mechanism distinct from a single design-freeze point in DBB forms. CCDC 14's GC 4.1 (Cash Allowances) and GC 4.2 (Contingency Allowance) mirror CCDC 2/3/5B's deferral mechanism.

codebook.label: Definition of Work/Products Scope for Off-Site Components
codebook.definition: Clause(s) defining 'Work', 'Products', materials and equipment to determine whether prefabricated modules and off-site-manufactured components are unambiguously covered.
codebook.memo: Combines T2, T3 and T5 codes on 'Ambiguity in contractual definition of Products/modules' and related sub-codes. GC 1.1.1-1.1.2 in CCDC 2/CcQ and CCDC 3's GC 1.1.1 are the anchor clauses. CCDC 5A defers this to separate CCDC 17 agreements. CCDC 5B's GC 1.1.1 parallels CCDC 2/3. CCDC 14's GC 1.1.1 extends this anchor to expressly include 'the design' as part of the Contract Documents' intended scope ('the design, the labour, the Products and other services necessary for the design and performance of the Work'), reflecting the design-build model's bundling of design and construction deliverables; no modular/off-site-specific refinement of 'Products' is present.

codebook.label: Progress/Final Payment and Certification for Off-Site Fabrication
codebook.definition: Payment clauses (progress payment, certification for payment, final payment) evaluated for their fit with off-site manufacture, including milestone payment for manufactured-but-undelivered/uninstalled modules.
codebook.memo: Merges T2, T3, T5 and T6 payment-mechanism codes. GC 5.2.3/5.2.8 in CCDC 2/CcQ; GC 5.5 (Deferred Work) in CcQ; CCDC 3's GC 5.3.3/5.3.7 and GC 5.9.1; CCDC 5A defers Work payment to CCDC 17; CCDC 5B's GC 5.4.3/5.4.9-A and GC 5.8.1. CCDC 14's GC 5.2.3 and GC 5.2.8 parallel these mechanics but explicitly extend the payment basis to include 'the value...of the Design Services and of the Work performed,' reflecting the bundled design-construction payment stream unique to the design-build form; GC 2.4.1 confirms the Payment Certifier certifies 'the value of the Design Services and of Work performed and Products delivered.'

codebook.label: Retention and Liquidated Damages Provisions
codebook.definition: Standard retention holdback and liquidated damages clauses assessed for their fit with off-site production schedules and manufacturer risk exposure.
codebook.memo: Drawn from T5's 'Retention and liquidated damages misalignment' code. CCDC 2's GC 5.4; CCDC 2 CcQ's GC 5.4 legal-hypothec variant; CCDC 3's GC 5.6.4/5.6.5 dual-jurisdiction mechanics; CCDC 5A's generic reference; CCDC 5B's GC 5.6. CCDC 14's GC 5.5 (Payment of Holdback Upon Substantial Performance) and GC 5.6 (Progressive Release of Holdback) parallel CCDC 2/3/5B's holdback regimes, including the common-law/Quebec bifurcation (GC 5.5.4-5.5.5); no stipulated liquidated damages clause is present, consistent with other CCDC forms reviewed.

codebook.label: Variation/Change Order Valuation and Scope-Limitation Clause
codebook.definition: Provisions defining how variations are valued, limiting the scope of instructable changes, and specifying (or omitting) a contractor's right to decline variations, including valuation of off-site production and expediting costs attributable to a change.
codebook.include_when: Apply when a clause sets out the method, cost basis, or scope boundary for pricing or authorizing a change, including cost categories that expressly cover shop/factory labour, expediting, or transportation attributable to the change.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to clauses solely concerning the timing/finalization of design (see C3) or to schedule-deviation incentive/penalty clauses unconnected to a formal change instrument (see C30). In cost-reimbursable/GMP CM forms, do not apply to the reimbursable Cost-of-the-Work categories which are baseline reimbursable cost items rather than change-valuation mechanics; code those under C37 instead.
codebook.memo: Combines T2, T5 and T11 variation-valuation codes. GC 6.3.7 in CCDC 2/CcQ explicitly includes shop/expediting labour costs. CCDC 3/5B embed this instead in the Cost of the Work definition (see C37 boundary). CCDC 5A addresses changes generically without cost-category detail. CCDC 14's GC 6.3.6-6.3.7 (Change Directive valuation based on the Design-Builder's actual expenditures/savings) parallels CCDC 2's structure, situating shop/factory labour and expediting cost recovery directly within the change-valuation mechanism itself (as in the stipulated-price forms) rather than within a separate baseline Cost-of-the-Work definition as in CCDC 3/5B.

codebook.label: Value Engineering Benefit-Sharing Clause
codebook.definition: Clause governing how cost savings from contractor-proposed value engineering/efficiency proposals are shared between owner and contractor.
codebook.memo: From T2 and T5 'Value Engineering Benefit-Sharing' codes. CCDC 2/CcQ, CCDC 3, CCDC 5A and CCDC 5B contain no explicit VE-proposal benefit-sharing clause; CCDC 5B's GMP Plus Percentage Cost Savings Option is a related but distinct pricing-basis mechanism (see C37). CCDC 14 likewise contains no value-engineering benefit-sharing clause; absence is a valid comparative result consistent with the other CCDC forms reviewed, notwithstanding the Design-Builder's structural incentive (as integrator of design and construction) to propose efficiencies within its fixed Contract Price.

codebook.label: Differing Site Conditions and Force Majeure Clause
codebook.definition: Provisions allocating risk for unforeseen physical site conditions and force majeure events, assessed for relevance where fabrication is decoupled from site.
codebook.memo: From T2's 'Differing Site Conditions and Force Majeure' code. GC 6.4/6.5.3 anchors recur in CCDC 2/CcQ and CCDC 3. CCDC 5A lacks a dedicated clause. CCDC 5B's GC 6.4/6.5.3 parallel CCDC 2/3. CCDC 14's GC 6.4 (Concealed or Unknown Conditions) and GC 6.5.3 (labour disputes, fire, weather, causes beyond the Design-Builder's control) are materially identical in structure to CCDC 2/3/5B's equivalent clauses, confirming recurrence of this clause type in the design-build form.

codebook.label: Changes in Law Clause
codebook.definition: Provision (or absence thereof) addressing compensation/adjustment when applicable law changes during the contract term.
codebook.memo: From T2 and T5 'Changes in Law' codes. GC 10.2.7 anchors recur in CCDC 2/CcQ and CCDC 3 (routed through GC 6.6). CCDC 5A has no dedicated clause. CCDC 5B's GC 10.2.7-A parallels CCDC 2/3. CCDC 14's GC 10.2.7 (claims for changes to laws/codes after proposal/bid closing, routed through the GC 6.6 claims mechanism) parallels CCDC 2/3/5B's equivalent provision, confirming this mechanism recurs in the design-build form.

codebook.label: Risk Allocation Fairness and Disclaimer Clauses
codebook.definition: General-conditions provisions and disclaimer language that transfer unforeseen or unpredictable risk unilaterally to one party (typically the contractor).
codebook.memo: Merges T2, T5 and T8 risk-transfer/disclaimer codes. GC 3.1.2/1.1.4 in CCDC 2/CcQ; CCDC 3's GC 3.1.3/3.4.1; CCDC 5A's GC 2.1.3/10.2.1 capped fee-linked liability; CCDC 5B's GC 1.1.4/3.1.3 and GC 13.2.1 contract-price-linked cap. CCDC 14's GC 3.1.2 (Design-Builder solely responsible for means/methods) and GC 2.1.2-2.1.3 (Design-Builder entitled to rely on Owner-supplied information; not responsible for design errors in Owner-supplied designs/Specifications absent acceptance) are the relevant balancing clauses. Distinctively, CCDC 14 establishes a two-tier liability-cap structure: GC 12.2.2 sets a general liability cap (insurance limit, or the greater of the Contract Price/$2,000,000 up to $20,000,000), while GC 12.3.1 sets a separate, narrower cap specifically for claims arising from the Design Services, limited to insurance coverage and to errors of the Consultant/Other Consultants -- a distinctive risk-allocation architecture unique among the CCDC forms reviewed, reflecting the design-build model's bundling of design and construction risk, and cross-referenced to new code C39 (design liability insurance).

codebook.label: General Conditions vs Particular Conditions Amendment Practice
codebook.definition: How particular/supplementary conditions modify, clarify or unbalance the risk allocation set by the general conditions, including employer-driven unfavorable amendments.
codebook.memo: Combines T2, T5 and T11 amendment-practice codes. GC 1.1.5/1.1.7.1/1.1.1/1.1.5 document-priority anchors recur across CCDC 2/CcQ, CCDC 3, CCDC 5A and CCDC 5B. CCDC 14's GC 1.1.6 sets a materially identical priority order (Agreement, Definitions, Supplementary Conditions, General Conditions, Owner's Statement of Requirements, Construction Documents), confirming the amendment-practice mechanism recurs across the full CCDC suite including the design-build form.

codebook.label: Transportation, Storage and Transit Insurance Clause
codebook.definition: Clauses addressing lead-time, transport/lifting limitations, storage, and insurance coverage for modules/components between factory and site.
codebook.memo: Merges T2, T3, T6, T8 and T13 logistics/transit codes. CCDC 2/CcQ, CCDC 3, CCDC 5A and CCDC 5B all lack a dedicated logistics/transit clause beyond generic references to 'transportation' as a provided facility or reimbursable cost item. CCDC 14 likewise contains no dedicated transit/logistics/insurance clause beyond the generic reference to 'transportation' as a Design-Builder-provided facility (GC 3.8.1); absence of a dedicated logistics clause is a valid comparative result consistent with all other CCDC forms reviewed.

codebook.label: Quality Assurance, Certification and Inspection Regime Clause
codebook.definition: Contractual mechanisms specifying manufacturer self-certification, third-party/factory certification, mock-up approval and inspection processes for off-site components, including access rights for review/inspection of work in preparation at locations other than the Place of the Work.
codebook.include_when: Apply when a clause establishes testing, inspection, certification, or access rights for reviewing work quality, whether at the Place of the Work or at an off-site fabrication location.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to clauses solely concerning document/design review of submittals prior to fabrication (see C36) or to supply-chain traceability documentation absent an inspection/certification function (see C15).
codebook.memo: Draws on T8, T7 and T6 QA/certification codes. GC 2.3.1 in CCDC 2/CcQ and CCDC 3 explicitly extends factory-access review rights; CCDC 5A lacks this; CCDC 5B's GC 2.4.1 parallels CCDC 2/3. CCDC 14's GC 3.1.10 explicitly requires the Design-Builder to provide access to 'the Work, including parts being performed at locations other than the Place of the Work,' directly paralleling CCDC 2/3/5B's factory-access QA provisions and confirming this MMC-relevant clause type recurs in the design-build form; GC 3.1.11 supports this with notice requirements for tests/inspections.

codebook.label: Chain of Custody and Component Traceability Clause
codebook.definition: Provisions requiring tracking/identification technologies and documented responsibility transfer for components moving through the fabrication-to-installation supply chain.
codebook.memo: From T8's 'Traceability, Chain of Custody' category. CCDC 2/CcQ, CCDC 3, CCDC 5A and CCDC 5B all contain no such mechanism. CCDC 14 likewise contains no explicit component-traceability or chain-of-custody mechanism; absence is a valid comparative result consistent with all other CCDC forms reviewed.

codebook.label: BIM/Digital Model Authorship, Ownership and Licensing Clause
codebook.definition: Provisions clarifying ownership, authorship and licensing of BIM/digital model data, and whether 2D drawings or 3D models constitute the binding contract document.
codebook.memo: Merges T5, T8 and T11 BIM/DfMA codes. GC 1.1.10-1.1.11 in CCDC 2/CcQ; CCDC 3's GC 1.1.9-1.1.10; CCDC 5A has no such clause; CCDC 5B's GC 1.1.10-1.1.11 parallel CCDC 2/3. CCDC 14's GC 1.1.7-1.1.10 address ownership/copyright of the Consultant's or Other Consultant's plans, Drawings, electronic media and models -- notably vesting copyright in the Consultant/Other Consultants (not the Design-Builder or Owner) and prohibiting Owner alteration -- a more elaborated ownership regime than CCDC 2/3/5B given the design-build model's reliance on a Design-Builder-retained Consultant, but still without addressing BIM/digital model authorship, licensing, or 2D-vs-3D bindingness specifically; this gap is a valid comparative result.

codebook.label: Liability Allocation for Digital Fabrication and Design-Model Defects
codebook.definition: Clause-level allocation of liability between designer, general contractor and fabricator for defects traceable to upstream digital models versus downstream fabrication.
codebook.memo: Combines T5 and T8 digital-fabrication-liability codes. CCDC 2/CcQ, CCDC 3 and CCDC 5B rely on their Shop Drawing regimes (see C36) as the paper/PDF-based analogue; CCDC 5A has no such regime. CCDC 14 contains no BIM/digital-model-specific liability clause; its Shop Drawing regime (GC 3.10.5, see C36) and its distinct design-services liability cap (GC 12.3.1, see C11/C39) are the relevant analogues, confirming the same absence-of-digital-model-liability-clause finding as other CCDC forms while highlighting the design-build form's additional design-liability layer not present in traditional DBB or CM forms.

codebook.label: IPD/Multiparty Agreement and Shared Risk-Reward Mechanisms
codebook.definition: Contractual features unique to Integrated Project Delivery and alliance-style agreements: multiparty signature, shared risk/reward pools, joint governance and target-cost/pain-gain sharing.
codebook.memo: Merges T2, T5, T9, T1 and T3 IPD/alliance codes. CCDC 2/CcQ, CCDC 3, CCDC 5A and CCDC 5B are all bilateral, non-IPD agreements notwithstanding cost-target or savings-sharing analogues. CCDC 14 is likewise a bilateral Owner-Design-Builder agreement (Article A-1) with no multiparty signature, shared risk-reward pool, or joint-governance mechanism; absence of IPD/alliance features is a valid comparative result consistent with all other CCDC forms reviewed, notwithstanding that the design-build structure itself achieves a degree of design-construction integration through single-party contracting rather than multiparty governance.

codebook.label: Suspension and Termination Provisions
codebook.definition: Clauses governing notice periods, discretion and consequences for suspension or termination of the contract, assessed for ambiguity/asymmetry.
codebook.memo: From T2's 'Suspension and Termination Ambiguity' sub-code. CCDC 2's GC 7.1/7.2, CCDC 2 CcQ's Civil Code overlay, CCDC 3's GC 7.1/7.2, CCDC 5A's estimate-class-based compensation, and CCDC 5B's phase-differentiated compensation are all documented. CCDC 14 introduces a distinctive pre-Work-commencement suspension/termination mechanism at GC 7.1, applicable specifically 'before the Work commences at the Place of the Work' (GC 7.1.1-7.1.4): if the Design Services are suspended beyond 20 Working Days and the parties do not agree to continue, the Owner is deemed to have terminated the Contract, entitling the Design-Builder to payment for Design Services performed plus damages including reasonable profit -- a design-phase-specific termination compensation mechanism distinct from, though conceptually related to, CCDC 5B's phase-differentiated compensation split. GC 7.2 (Owner's termination for default/insolvency) and GC 7.3 (Design-Builder's termination rights) parallel CCDC 2/3/5B's symmetric structures.

codebook.label: Liability Allocation Among Multiple Contracting Parties
codebook.definition: General clauses defining liability boundaries among owner, designer, contractor, manufacturer and subcontractors, particularly in multiparty or fragmented arrangements.
codebook.memo: From T2's 'Liability Allocation Clarity' sub-code. GC 1.1.6/1.1.2 privity anchors recur in CCDC 2/CcQ and CCDC 3; CCDC 5A's fragmented agency structure; CCDC 5B's GC 1.1.6. CCDC 14's GC 1.1.2 (no contractual relationship between Owner and Consultant, Other Consultant, Subcontractor, Supplier or their agents/employees) is the parallel foundational privity clause, notably extended here to expressly include the Consultant, reflecting that the Consultant is contracted by the Design-Builder rather than the Owner in this design-build structure.

codebook.label: Dispute Resolution, Claims and Extension-of-Time Handling
codebook.definition: Provisions governing claim submission, EOT requests, tiered dispute resolution mechanisms and their administration.
codebook.memo: Merges T2's EOT/dispute-related codes. CCDC 2's Part 8, CCDC 2 CcQ's Project Mediator mechanism, CCDC 3's GC 8.2, CCDC 5A's Part 7 and CCDC 5B's Part 8 all establish materially similar tiered dispute mechanisms. CCDC 14's Part 8 (Negotiation, Mediation and Arbitration) requires appointment of a Project Mediator under CCDC 40 within 20 Working Days (GC 8.1.5), followed by mediation and arbitration (GC 8.1.6-8.1.9), with statutory lien rights preserved without waiver of arbitration rights (GC 8.2.2) -- materially identical to CCDC 3/5A/5B's tiered structure, confirming this mechanism is now standard across current-generation CCDC forms including the design-build form.

codebook.label: Contract Drafting Clarity, Readability and Consistency
codebook.definition: The linguistic/structural quality of contract text—jargon, sentence complexity, visual aids, internal contradictions—as it affects interpretability and dispute risk.
codebook.memo: Merges T2, T5 and T11 drafting-quality codes. CCDC 5A's GC 7.1.6-7.1.8 and CCDC 5B's GC 8.3.6 illustrate internal drafting fragmentation. CCDC 14's Part 12 (Indemnification, Limitation of Liability, Waiver of Claims and Warranty) is a lengthy, cross-referential drafting structure (GC 12.1-12.5, including layered claim-notice-timing provisions at GC 12.4.9-12.4.10) illustrating the kind of complex, cross-referencing drafting this code is designed to capture when assessing interpretability across CCDC forms.

codebook.label: Communication and Collaboration Protocol Clauses
codebook.definition: Contract terms mandating communication turnaround (RFI/submittal timelines), data-sharing protocols, and collaborative decision-making structures between offsite and onsite parties.
codebook.memo: Combines T2, T7 and T9 communication/collaboration codes. Article A-6/A-9/A-7 notice-formality anchors recur across CCDC 2/CcQ, CCDC 3 and CCDC 5A/5B, generally lacking MMC-specific collaboration protocols. CCDC 14's Article A-6 (Notices in Writing) parallels these; GC 2.2.2 and GC 2.4.6 additionally require that all communications between the Owner/Payment Certifier and the Consultant, Other Consultant, Subcontractor or Supplier be forwarded through the Design-Builder, establishing a centralized-communication-channel requirement analogous to CCDC 5A's GC 3.1.1.8 -- a relevant, if generic, collaboration-structuring provision reflecting the Design-Builder's single-point coordination role.

codebook.label: Subcontract Flow-Down and Supply Chain Risk Transfer
codebook.definition: Provisions governing how risk, cost and obligations flow down from general contractor to subcontractors, suppliers and manufacturers, including power asymmetries, upstream risk transfer, absence of contractual privity between Owner/Consultant and Subcontractors/Suppliers, and coordination obligations where manufactured components are supplied under separate contracts with Other Contractors.
codebook.include_when: Apply when a clause governs flow-down of contractual terms/risk to Subcontractors or Suppliers, denies privity between the Owner/Consultant and such parties, or governs coordination/cost consequences of work performed by Other Contractors or the Owner's own forces alongside the Contractor's Work.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to clauses solely concerning prequalification/selection criteria for the Contractor's own subcontractors absent a flow-down or coordination dimension (see C33).
codebook.memo: Merges T6, T9, T10, T12 and T13 supply-chain/flow-down codes. GC 1.1.6/3.2 in CCDC 2/CcQ; CCDC 3's GC 1.1.2/3.2.1-3.2.5; CCDC 5A's inverse agency-model structure; CCDC 5B's GC 1.1.6/3.2.1-3.2.6. CCDC 14's GC 1.1.2 (no privity) and GC 2.6 (Work by Owner or Other Contractors, including coordination duties at GC 2.6.2 and change-order consequences at GC 2.6.5) parallel CCDC 2/3/5B's equivalent provisions. GC 3.4.1 additionally requires the Design-Builder to flow down contract terms not only to Subcontractors/Suppliers but also to Other Consultants, and to be fully responsible for their acts -- an expanded flow-down scope reflecting the design-build model's incorporation of design-services subcontracting into the same risk-transfer framework as construction subcontracting.

codebook.label: Payment Security and Financial Guarantee Instruments
codebook.definition: Clauses providing for bonds, letters of credit, bank guarantees, back-to-back payment terms, or other instruments securing cash flow and non-performance risk.
codebook.memo: From T2 and T6 payment-security codes. CCDC 2/CcQ, CCDC 3 and CCDC 5B all defer bonding to separately referenced bond documents; CCDC 5A's GC 3.1.1.7-type provision runs Owner-to-CM. CCDC 14's GC 11.2.1-11.2.2 address Contract security only where 'specified in the Contract Documents,' referencing CCDC-approved bond forms rather than mandating bonding directly in the General Conditions, consistent with CCDC 2/3/5B's approach. GC 5.1.1 (Financing Information Required of the Owner) parallels CCDC 3's/5A's Owner-to-Design-Builder financing-assurance provisions.

codebook.label: Automated/Smart Contract Payment and Penalty Enforcement Provisions
codebook.definition: Contractual or supplementary provisions enabling blockchain/smart-contract-based automated payment, real-time incentive/penalty enforcement, and their governance limitations regarding change orders.
codebook.memo: Merges T3, T4 and T11 automated-contract codes. CCDC 2/CcQ, CCDC 3, CCDC 5A and CCDC 5B all contain no such provisions. CCDC 14 likewise contains no automated/blockchain-based payment or penalty enforcement provisions; absence is a valid comparative result consistent with other CCDC forms reviewed.

codebook.label: Inflation and Price Escalation Adjustment Clause
codebook.definition: Provisions (or their absence) allowing price adjustment for material/labour cost inflation, and use of off-site bulk procurement as a hedging strategy.
codebook.memo: From T3 and T10 inflation/price-volatility codes. CCDC 2/CcQ's fixed Contract Price with tax/duty-only adjustment; CCDC 3's cost-reimbursable pass-through; CCDC 5A's percentage-fee tracking; CCDC 5B's hybrid structure. CCDC 14's GC 10.1.1-10.1.2 fix the Contract Price inclusive of taxes/duties in effect at proposal/bid closing, with adjustment only for changes in included taxes/duties (via the GC 6.6 claims mechanism), not general material/labour inflation -- confirming the same gap identified in CCDC 2, consistent with its stipulated-price structure.

codebook.label: Regulatory Compliance and Code/Standards Reference Clause
codebook.definition: Clauses requiring compliance with applicable building codes, modular-specific standards, and government mandates, and addressing gaps where such codes/standards do not yet exist for MMC.
codebook.memo: Merges T1, T8, T10 and T13 regulatory/standards-gap codes. GC 10.2 in CCDC 2/CcQ and CCDC 3 is generic; CCDC 5A lacks an equivalent clause; CCDC 5B's GC 10.2 parallels CCDC 2/3. CCDC 14's GC 10.2.1-10.2.7 (Laws, Notices, Permits and Fees) is materially identical in structure to CCDC 2/3/5B's GC 10.2, drafted generically without reference to modular-specific standards, and notably allocates responsibility for verifying the Owner's Statement of Requirements' code-compliance away from the Design-Builder (GC 10.2.5) while still requiring the Design-Builder to comply with codes affecting the Design Services/Work (GC 10.2.4).

codebook.label: Labour and Union Provisions Affecting Off-Site Work Allocation
codebook.definition: Contractual or side-agreement provisions addressing labour union jurisdiction, work-hour allocation, and human-robot collaboration in the shift of work off-site.
codebook.memo: From T6, T9 and T12 labour/union codes. GC 6.5.3.1 in CCDC 2/CcQ, CCDC 3 and CCDC 5B functions only as a delay-excusing event; CCDC 5A has no analogue. CCDC 14's GC 6.5.3.1 references labour disputes, strikes and lock-outs only as a delay-excusing event, not as a work-allocation mechanism, materially identical to CCDC 2/3/5B's equivalent provision.

codebook.label: Delivery Schedule Deviation Incentive/Penalty Mechanism
codebook.definition: Clauses (static or dynamic) allocating cost and responsibility for deviations between planned and actual component delivery/production schedules, including reward-penalty structures.
codebook.memo: Merges T3, T6 and T4 schedule-deviation codes. CCDC 2's GC 3.4, CCDC 3's GC 3.5, CCDC 5A's Construction Schedule reference, and CCDC 5B's GC 3.4 all contain no component-delivery-specific incentive/penalty mechanism. CCDC 14's GC 3.6.1 (Design Services and Work Schedule) requires a schedule and monthly monitoring but likewise contains no component-delivery-specific incentive/penalty mechanism, consistent with all other CCDC forms reviewed.

codebook.label: Product-Based/Framework and Serial Contracting Structures
codebook.definition: Contractual models moving away from single-project agreements toward long-term framework, serial-tendering or product-warranty-style contracts suited to repeatable manufactured products.
codebook.memo: From T1's 'Product-Based and Non-Traditional Delivery Models' category. CCDC 2/CcQ, CCDC 3, CCDC 5A and CCDC 5B are all single-project agreements. CCDC 14 is likewise drafted as a single-project design-build agreement (Article A-1); absence of framework/serial contracting structures is a valid comparative result consistent with all other CCDC forms reviewed.

codebook.label: Insurance and Warranty Coverage for Prefabricated Components
codebook.definition: Provisions defining insurance coverage (including during transport/storage) and warranty/guarantee obligations specific to manufactured and prefabricated components, including gaps arising from coverage/protection language framed around the 'Place of the Work.'
codebook.include_when: Apply when a clause defines insurance coverage scope, warranty obligations, or protection-of-work responsibility as they bear on manufactured/prefabricated components, including where such coverage is ambiguous for components located off-site.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to clauses solely concerning transit logistics/scheduling without an insurance or warranty dimension (see C13).
codebook.memo: Combines T5, T8 and T13 insurance/warranty codes. GC 9.1.1/11.1.1.4/12.4 in CCDC 2/CcQ; CCDC 3's parallel anchors plus Civil Code overlay; CCDC 5A's multi-tier wrap-up regime; CCDC 5B's elaborated regime closer to 5A. CCDC 14's GC 9.1.1 (Protection of Work and Property) and GC 11.1.1 (general liability, automobile, aircraft/watercraft, 'all risks' property, boiler/machinery, equipment, and professional liability insurance, jointly naming Owner, Consultant, Other Consultants, Owner's Advisor and Payment Certifier as insureds) establish a more elaborated regime than CCDC 2/3, closer to CCDC 5A/5B's multi-party structure, but still framed around the Place of the Work and 'the Work,' leaving the same off-site fabrication-facility/in-transit coverage ambiguity identified across the CCDC suite. GC 12.5 (Warranty) parallels CCDC 2/3/5B's one-year warranty anchor. The dedicated professional liability insurance requirement (GC 11.1.1.9) is a design-build-specific addition, now more precisely captured under new code C39 alongside the related design-services liability cap (GC 12.3.1).

codebook.label: Contractor/Manufacturer Qualification and Selection Criteria
codebook.definition: Provisions or procurement criteria governing how contractors, fabricators and manufacturers are prequalified or selected, including alternatives to lowest-bid selection and Owner objection/substitution rights over proposed Subcontractors or Suppliers.
codebook.include_when: Apply when a clause governs the process by which a Subcontractor, Supplier, fabricator or manufacturer is nominated, identified, objected to, or substituted, including associated price/time adjustment consequences.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to clauses governing ongoing flow-down of contractual risk/terms once a Subcontractor or Supplier is engaged (see C24).
codebook.memo: From T2's 'Lowest-Bid Contractor Selection' and T1's 'Feasibility scoring and selection tools'. GC 3.6.2-3.6.5 in CCDC 2/CcQ; CCDC 3's GC 3.7.2-3.7.4; CCDC 5A defers to CCDC 17; CCDC 5B's GC 3.6.2-3.6.6-A. CCDC 14's GC 3.4.2-3.4.5 establish a mechanism closely paralleling CCDC 2/3/5B's Subcontractor/Supplier nomination-objection-substitution provisions, but distinctively extend it to 'Other Consultants' as well, with price/time adjustment consequences for Owner-required changes (GC 3.4.4) -- reflecting the design-build model's incorporation of design-services subcontracting into the same qualification/selection framework as construction subcontracting.

codebook.label: Vertical Integration/Single-Entity Contracting Model
codebook.definition: Contractual recognition (or non-recognition) of business models where design, manufacture and construction are delivered by a single integrated entity, redefining traditional party roles.
codebook.memo: From T1, T7 and T9 vertical-integration codes. CCDC 2/CcQ, CCDC 3, CCDC 5A and CCDC 5B all assume separate Owner/Consultant/Contractor(or CM/Trade Contractor) roles; absence of vertical-integration recognition is a valid comparative result. CCDC 14 sits at an intermediate point on the integration spectrum: while it establishes single-point design-build responsibility (see C1), the Consultant remains a separate contracting party retained by the Design-Builder under a CCDC 15-based agreement (GC 3.1.3-3.1.4) rather than an in-house function of a single vertically integrated firm. This is a materially different point from true single-firm vertical integration (design, manufacture and construction all performed by one entity with no separate consultant contract), though closer to it than CCDC 2/3/5A/5B's fully separated structures -- a useful intermediate comparator for the delivery-integration spectrum this code tracks.

codebook.label: Scope of Work, Roles and Responsibilities Definition Clause
codebook.definition: Provisions clearly (or unclearly) defining scope of work, stakeholder roles, and references to multiple manufacturers/suppliers in DfMA and prefabrication contexts.
codebook.memo: From T5's 'Unclear scope, roles, and responsibilities in DfMA contracts' and related T13 codes. GC 1.1.1-1.1.3 anchors recur across CCDC 2/CcQ, CCDC 3 and CCDC 5B; CCDC 5A's GC 2.1.1-2.1.6/3.1.1 define a genuinely multi-actor structure. CCDC 14's GC 1.1.1-1.1.3 are the parallel anchors, extended to include 'design' given the design-build structure, but drafted without specific reference to multiple manufacturers/suppliers or prefabrication-context role allocation, consistent with other CCDC forms reviewed.

codebook.label: Shop Drawing/Submittal Review and Design-Responsibility Transfer Clause
codebook.definition: Provisions governing the preparation, submission timing, and Consultant review of Shop Drawings and other submittals, and the allocation of responsibility between Contractor and Consultant/Owner for errors, omissions or deviations disclosed (or not disclosed) through that review process.
codebook.include_when: Apply when a clause addresses the submission, review, approval, or liability consequences of Shop Drawings/submittals, including the scope and limits of a Consultant's or Owner's review (e.g., 'design concept only') and the Contractor's retained responsibility for accuracy.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to clauses concerning BIM/digital model authorship, ownership or licensing absent a submittal-review dimension (see C16); do not apply to inspection/testing/certification of physical work or components (see C14); do not apply to liability allocation for defects specifically traceable to digital fabrication models (see C17).
codebook.memo: New code capturing GC 3.8/3.10 Shop Drawing regimes across CCDC 2/3/5B; CCDC 5A lacks this regime. CCDC 14's GC 3.10.1-3.10.5 establish a fully elaborated Shop Drawing regime paralleling CCDC 2/3/5B's equivalent provisions, confirming the Owner's review is 'for conformity to the intent of the Contract Documents and for general arrangement only' and does not relieve the Design-Builder of responsibility for errors or omissions (GC 3.10.5) -- a design-build-specific rewording ('intent of the Contract Documents' rather than 'design concept') reflecting that the Design-Builder itself, rather than a separately-retained Owner's Consultant, holds primary design responsibility and thus frames the review standard against the whole Contract Documents rather than an externally-authored design concept.

codebook.label: Cost-Reimbursable Price Basis and Reimbursable Cost Categories Clause
codebook.definition: Provisions establishing a cost-plus-fee pricing structure (Cost of the Work plus Contractor's/Construction Manager's Fee), defining reimbursable cost categories (including shop/factory labour, expediting and transportation costs), and optional Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP), Target Contract Price, or GMP-plus-savings-sharing mechanisms that cap or benchmark the reimbursable price.
codebook.include_when: Apply when a clause defines the Cost of the Work, reimbursable cost categories, the Contractor's/Construction Manager's Fee structure (percentage or fixed) for performing the Work, or an optional GMP/Target Contract Price/savings-sharing mechanism that establishes the fundamental price basis of the Work, as distinct from clauses valuing subsequent changes to that price (see C7).
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to clauses solely concerning the valuation or authorization procedure for a change/variation once the baseline price basis is established (see C7); do not apply to progress/final payment certification and application timing mechanics (see C5); do not apply to a Construction Manager's Fee-for-Services compensation for a discrete advisory/pre-construction phase where that fee is not tied to performing or bearing cost risk for the Work itself (see C38).
codebook.memo: New code capturing CCDC 3's Articles A-4 through A-7 and CCDC 5B's Articles A-7 through A-10. CCDC 5A does not fit (see C38). CCDC 14 does not fit this code: Article A-4 establishes a stipulated Contract Price rather than a Cost-of-the-Work-plus-Fee structure, and the form contains no GMP/Target Contract Price/savings-sharing option; CCDC 14 is a stipulated-price form comparable to CCDC 2 in this respect, notwithstanding its design-build delivery structure -- absence of a cost-reimbursable pricing architecture is a valid comparative result.

codebook.label: Agency/Phase-Specific Construction Manager Fee-for-Services Compensation Structure
codebook.definition: Provisions establishing the compensation of a Construction Manager (or similar agent/advisor) as a professional-services fee (time-based, fixed-fee, and/or percentage-of-cost) plus separately reimbursed expenses, for advisory/coordination Services, applicable either (a) to a fully non-risk-bearing agency-style Construction Manager where the Work is performed and priced under separate agreements with Trade Contractors, or (b) to a discrete pre-construction/advisory services phase within an otherwise at-risk delivery instrument, distinct from any subsequent Cost-of-the-Work-based compensation for the Work itself.
codebook.include_when: Apply when a clause defines a Construction Manager's or similar agent/advisor's fee structure (time-based rates, fixed fee, or percentage fee tied to a cost benchmark) and/or its reimbursable expenses for providing advisory/coordination Services, whether (a) the Work is performed and priced under separate agreements with Trade Contractors or a Contractor not party to the instrument being coded, or (b) the clause compensates a discrete pre-construction/advisory services phase within an otherwise at-risk delivery instrument, even where that same Construction Manager bears cost risk for the Work itself under a separate phase/article of the same instrument (see C37).
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to clauses establishing a cost-reimbursable price basis for the Work itself (Cost of the Work plus Contractor's/Construction Manager's Fee, with or without a GMP/Target Contract Price/savings-sharing option), which remain coded under C37; do not apply to progress/final payment certification and application timing mechanics generally (see C5).
codebook.memo: New code capturing CCDC 5A's Article A-5 and CCDC 5B's Article A-5/A-6. CCDC 14 does not fit this code: the Design-Builder is compensated via a stipulated Contract Price for both Design Services and Work (Article A-4/A-5), not via a professional-services fee structure for an agency/advisory role; the Design-Builder bears full performance responsibility and cost risk for both design and construction, distinguishing it from the agency-CM fee-for-services architecture this code targets. Absence is a valid comparative result confirming CCDC 14's stipulated-price, single-point-responsibility structure.

codebook.label: Design Liability Insurance and Design-Services Liability Cap Clause
codebook.definition: Provisions requiring dedicated professional/design liability (errors and omissions) insurance and/or establishing a liability cap specifically applicable to claims arising from Design Services, distinct from the general liability insurance and cap applicable to construction Work.
codebook.include_when: Apply when a clause mandates professional liability/design errors-and-omissions insurance coverage for a party performing or responsible for design, or establishes a liability limitation specifically tied to design-services claims (as opposed to a general liability cap covering the Work as a whole).
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to general liability insurance or general liability caps covering construction Work risk without a design-specific carve-out (see C11, C32); do not apply to Shop Drawing/submittal review responsibility-transfer clauses absent an insurance or liability-cap dimension (see C36).
codebook.memo: New code added to capture CCDC 14's GC 11.1.1.9 (mandatory professional liability insurance for the Design-Builder, with minimum per-claim and aggregate limits, maintained for 2 years after Substantial Performance) and GC 12.3.1 (Limitation of Liability for Design Services, capping the Design-Builder's liability for claims arising from errors, omissions or negligent performance of the Design Services by the Consultant or Other Consultant to the amount of the required insurance). This dual mechanism is a direct product of the design-build delivery model's integration of design and construction risk within a single contracting party (see C1), and is absent from CCDC 2/3/5A/5B, where design responsibility for the Consultant's work typically sits outside the construction contract entirely (the Consultant being retained directly by the Owner rather than by the Contractor/Construction Manager). This is clause-level identifiable and comparatively useful (Rule 1-3): it lets researchers compare how different CCDC forms allocate and insure design risk for MMC/prefab projects where design and fabrication are closely coupled, and distinguishes design-specific liability treatment from the general risk-allocation/disclaimer code (C11) and general insurance/warranty code (C32).
